solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: For investment I'll borrow shillings as well, with almost nothing

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself in the first person; the definition describes the person rather than naming them

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shillings in old British money (£sd)
too means also, in addition

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: zero is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone planning to take out a loan to invest, alongside some shillings and next to no money of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: A stoozer borrows money at zero interest (typically on a credit card) and invests it, pocketing the interest. The clue is spoken in that person's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoozing is the practice of borrowing interest-free credit in order to deposit the money and earn interest on it.

clue.text: Religious mystic provided bone from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: if means provided that
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone

explanation.surface: A holy man offering a bone, approaching from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofi is a variant spelling of Sufi, a follower of the Islamic mystical tradition.

clue.text: Bend too much in full view when back of garment yields to pressure

indicators.note: one letter gives way so that another takes its place

parts.note: overtly means openly, done for all to see

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, supplying its final letter
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone bending over too far in public, when the back of their clothing gives under the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers, to overply is to ply, that is to bend or work, excessively.

clue.text: Chipmunk of variable proportions apart from small and large

parts.note: Z is one of the letters algebra uses for a variable

indicators.note: apart from means leaving out, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: proportions here means dimensions, or size
S is the clothing abbreviation for small
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A chipmunk of no fixed dimensions, neither small nor large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small and large' look like a pair to be removed together, but only S goes; L is then added.
explanation.definitionFit: The zizel is a ground squirrel or suslik, a close relative of the chipmunk; Chambers loosely equates them.

clue.text: Coolness in R&B, always for poetry's sake?

definitions.text: Coolness in R&B, always for poetry's sake?

indicators.note: one thing set in another, here the word for coolness sits between the two letters

parts.note: the two letters are taken from R&B, with the ampersand dropped
ice is extreme coolness
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Music fans wanting rhythm and blues to stay cool forever, at least in verse.
explanation.walkthrough: R&B is read as standing for its own two letters. The whole clue also hints at the answer, R&B suggesting rice and beer together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from fermented rice, such as Japanese sake, which the clue's last word slyly points to.

clue.text: Mark taking in jaunt slaughtered small deer

indicators.note: taking in means containing, so the outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: MK is the abbreviation for mark, as in the old German currency or a model number

indicators.note: slaughtered suggests something knocked to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word jaunt, a pleasure trip, supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark brings down a small deer while out on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The muntjac or muntjak is a small Asian deer, now also feral in Britain, known as the barking deer.

clue.text: Drug carrier volunteers as red rag to a bull?

definitions.note: the question mark flags that the idiom is meant literally here

parts.note: a mule is someone who smuggles drugs
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler and volunteers whose activities provoke fury, like a red rag to a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red rag to a bull' reads as the idiom for provocation, but it is literal: the matador's cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The muleta is the red cloth a matador waves on a stick to guide the bull in the final stage of a bullfight.

clue.text: Egg cases repelled noise? I accept that, thanks

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: din is loud noise
amen means so be it, an assent
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone turning back a noisy complaint, agreeing and saying thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Nidamenta are the protective capsules or ribbons that hold the eggs of molluscs and other invertebrates; the singular is nidamentum.

clue.text: Sailor shortened gun with duplication in underwater jet system

indicators.note: shortened means cut, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: jack, as in Jack tar, is a sailor
the Uzi submachine gun, with its middle letter doubled

explanation.surface: A sailor whose gun has been cut down and doubled, used in an underwater weapon system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwater jet system' suggests military hardware, but the jets are the bubbling water of a whirlpool bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacuzzi is a whirlpool bath in which jets of water are forced through the tub beneath the surface.

clue.text: Selling direct to Europe affected only Denmark's extremists and ruler

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word only is taken letter for letter as part of the anagram material
the first and last letters of the country's name; DK is also Denmark's international code
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Danish extremists and their monarch hit by direct exports to Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Klondyking, in Chambers, is selling fish directly from British boats to factory ships, originally for export to Europe.

clue.text: Commonwealth member in charge splits following American quite agitated

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the pair of letters breaks the other word apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: real is American informal for very or quite
NZ, New Zealand, is a Commonwealth country

explanation.surface: A Commonwealth official comes between an American and someone very upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzical is an old word for frenzied or frantic, wildly worked up.

clue.text: Knock down old butcher's

definitions.note: rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so this is a noun for a glance

parts.note: to deck someone is to knock them to the floor

explanation.surface: An old butcher's shop being demolished.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang for a look (butcher's hook = look); it is not a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Decko, or dekko, is British slang for a quick look, the same meaning as a butcher's.

clue.text: Wasting time in pub in Paris, the lowest one, last character bled

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house
le is French for the

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so one letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: the bottom is the lowest part
I is the Roman numeral for one
zed, the letter Z, is the last character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone frittering away time in a Parisian bar, at their lowest ebb, finally drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter is used as its spelt name, ZED, rather than Z.
explanation.definitionFit: To phlebotomize is to let blood from a vein, the old medical practice of bleeding a patient.

clue.text: Second bit of language on editor's printout unaffected by cuts?

parts.note: a word is a small unit of language
a proof is a trial printing for an editor to check

explanation.surface: An editor checking a printed proof for a second word, hoping the text survives cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' reads as editorial cuts, but the cuts are made by a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Swordproof means able to resist a sword's slashes, so blade cuts do no harm.

clue.text: Tons more sensible as a measure of distance?

parts.note: way is informal for much or a lot, as tons is
wiser means more sensible

explanation.surface: Someone much more sensible, as judged by some yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A waywiser is an old instrument, a wheel with a counter, for measuring distance travelled along a road.

clue.text: So, hail spread about even is linked to matching rain

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other word
spread means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word so is taken as written into the anagram
the word hail joins it as letters to be rearranged
even and yet both mean still, as in even better or yet better

explanation.surface: Hail scatters about evenly, as if tied to the pattern of the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An isohyetal line on a map joins places that receive equal rainfall, so it relates to matching amounts of rain.

clue.text: Good stroke for curling hot part of lamp

parts.note: in means fashionable, as hot does
the wick is the part of a lamp that burns

explanation.surface: A well-played shot in curling, alongside the hot part of a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling is the Scottish sport of sliding stones on ice; 'curling' in the surface could also suggest the lamp's flame.
explanation.definitionFit: An inwick in curling is a shot that glances off another stone and slides in towards the target.

clue.text: Reptilian family beset by article probing generation

indicators.note: probing means poking into, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: an age is a generation or era
amid means surrounded by, as beset by does
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family of reptiles surrounded by journalists investigating a generation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agamidae are the family of lizards that includes agamas, dragon lizards and the frilled lizard.

clue.text: Whistle-blower depressed when tide turns?

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the noun, the ebb that comes as the tide turns

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle in sport
low means down in spirits

explanation.surface: A whistle-blower feeling down when the tide of opinion turns against them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but it is the sports official.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflow is the ebbing or flowing back of water, the outgoing movement after the tide turns.

clue.text: Female arrested in possession of ring is former lover

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so the round letter is placed inside

parts.note: ran in is informal for arrested
O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A woman caught carrying a ring that turns out to be from her old flame.
explanation.walkthrough: Former applies to the word itself: it is an archaic term.
explanation.definitionFit: Franion is an obsolete word for a paramour or gay companion, a lover in old literature.

clue.text: Good rebuke in a sweet thing Jesus said

indicators.note: these letters are set inside the other pair

parts.note: the word a is taken as written
hon, short for honey, is a sweet term of address
a rap is a sharp rebuke

explanation.surface: A kindly scolding delivered tenderly, like something Jesus once said.
explanation.definitionFit: An agraphon is a saying attributed to Jesus that is not recorded in the canonical Gospels.

clue.text: ANC leaving human chain in disarray as elements were called earlier

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun, a former element name

indicators.note: disarray means disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaving means departing, so those letters are removed

parts.note: the word human is used as written for its letters
the word chain is used as written for its letters
the three letters of ANC, the African National Congress, are struck out

explanation.surface: The ANC withdraws from a human chain protest, leaving it disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party, and here just three letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Hahnium was a proposed name, later dropped, for elements 105 and 108, now dubnium and hassium.

clue.text: In Glasgow, crazy guy runs up to pinch wife

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: pinching means grasping, so the letter is held inside
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a dude is a guy

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian madman dashes up to steal someone's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Redwud is a Scots form of reid-wud, meaning stark mad, the word used in Glasgow for furious.

clue.text: Perhaps dishy leader's position among the deficient could be a fluke

definitions.note: the fluke is one example of the class, signalled by could be

parts.note: platy means flat like a plate, and a dish is a kind of plate, so dishy is an example
the helm is where the leader steers from
in means among

indicators.note: deficient means lacking, so the word is a letter short

parts.note: the word the, as written, loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An attractive leader holding a place among the poor might just be a lucky chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluke' reads as a stroke of luck; it is the parasitic flatworm.
explanation.definitionFit: Platyhelminths are flatworms, a phylum that includes the parasitic flukes and tapeworms.

clue.text: Indian ravine protected by international law

indicators.note: the answer is sheltered within the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of international and the start of law

explanation.surface: An Indian valley safeguarded by the rules of international law.
explanation.definitionFit: A nalla or nullah is an Indian watercourse or ravine, often dry outside the rainy season.

clue.text: Ancient heavens spread evenly across Rio Grande

definitions.note: an old exclamation, as in good heavens

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters spread through the river's name are taken

parts.note: the river's name, whose second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are taken

explanation.surface: Old skies stretching evenly over the Rio Grande.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens' looks like skies, but it is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Igad is an archaic oath, a variant of egad, used like good heavens to express surprise.

clue.text: One who sees much potential in egg's round, endless prospect

definitions.text: One who sees much potential in egg

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a vista is a prospect or view

explanation.surface: An optimist eyes a round egg and sees endless possibilities in it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovist held the old theory that the egg contains the whole preformed organism, needing sperm only to trigger growth.

clue.text: Weather-changing event, mostly in short tapering form, rapidly changing direction for snow

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the verbal noun, the act of skiing in quick turns

indicators.note: the shortened weather word sits inside the other shortened word
short means cut, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a wedge is a shape that tapers to an edge

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: El Niño is the Pacific current that disrupts global weather

explanation.surface: A climate event, partly contained in a narrowing shape, swings the snow this way and that.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedeln is a skiing technique of short quick parallel turns, swinging the skis rapidly from side to side down the slope.

clue.text: Force joint daughter twisted in Perth

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force
the ankle is a joint
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter's ankle joint twisted by force on a trip to Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, flagging a Scots word; fankle is Scots for tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fankled is Scots for tangled or entangled, the sense of twisted used north of the border.

clue.text: Once covered in fat, work off with a welcoming gesture?

indicators.note: off means removed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: open-armed describes greeting someone with arms spread wide
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone formerly overweight, who now works it off and greets everyone warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: Once marks the definition as an obsolete sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives enarm as obsolete for to lard, so enarmed meant larded, coated with grease.
